title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
description: The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in Ameri
body: The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US. China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee. On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years. The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China. China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, has been reported to be one if its largest customers.Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take.The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

title: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after Trump says he 'made' the deal
description: The head of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI told the BBC that the Nvidia board must have been under "enormous pressure" from the
body: The head of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI told the BBC that the Nvidia board must have been under "enormous pressure" from the White House to reinstate Huang.Prof Stuart Russell, who is professor of computer science at UC Berkeley, said the stock price of Nvidia and similar firms has been a major factor in "underpinning US economic growth for years"."I assume the White House was worried that the markets would go down a lot further in the next few weeks unless they go him back in," he says.Trump's vocal backing of Huang comes despite the concerns of US lawmakers, including some Republicans, over the CEO's affair and Nvidia's compliance with US export controls. "Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang," Republican congressman Don Bacon of Nebraska said. "We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible."Sen Tom Cotton, fellow Republican who represents Arkansas, vowed that Congress would investigate. "The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it's not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back," he said. Democrats, who will control both chambers of Congress from January, have already promised to launch Nvidia investigations.Senator Elizabeth Warren, who is set to be chairwoman of the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement that the reinstatement was "reckless". Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a member of the House foreign affairs committee, also condemned the move in a statement to the BBC as "premature" before multiple investigations are concluded. Fellow Democratic Representative Andre Carson, a member of the House intelligence committee, told the BBC that "Congress needs a full accounting of whether any controlled technology was diverted" to China.Huang is scheduled to appear before Congress for a closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December. Two days later, he has been asked to testify before the Senate banking committee. Since returning last year to the White House, Trump has amassed a significant level of investment in Nvidia. Recent financial disclosures show he purchased $265,000 in its stock and sold as much as $15,000 worth of shares in September. A BBC review of his government financial disclosures for the last two years shows he  purchased shares of Nvidia stock worth between $23m and $86m (£18m and £66m). And he has bought Nvidia stock 85 separate times through a number of investment accounts.The value of those holdings would have been affected by the recent fall in Nvidia's stock price amid Huang's exit.Trump has also sold some of his stake in Nvidia since returning to the presidency. Over 19 sales, Trump gained between $3.5m and $10.2m, according to his government disclosures.The BBC has contacted the White House.Both Trump and White House have repeatedly rejected assertions that he has profited from the presidency. The president has said "everybody" was making money from rising stocks and he does not make decisions related to his investment accounts.The White House has emphasised that Trump has placed his businesses in a trust managed by his sons.With additional reporting from Brandon Drenon and Rachel Clun

schema.headline: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after Trump says he 'made' the deal
